audit_items.proof_trace: The resolved code_scope (process_slashings, L1782-1798) is a mismatch -- it only decreases balances for validators already flagged slashed and contains no justification or quorum logic; fallback-resolved via Grep/Read to the actual enforcement chain. weigh_justification_and_finalization (L1509-1549) only sets current_justified_checkpoint for an epoch when attesting balance * 3 >= total_active_balance * 2 (L1524, L1529), so any two distinct checkpoints justified at the same target epoch each required >=2/3 of stake; two such quorums necessarily intersect by >=1/3 of stake (2/3+2/3>1). Each validator in that intersection has, by definition, cast attestations for two different checkpoints at the same target epoch, which is_slashable_attestation_data (L749-760) classifies as a double vote (or surround vote); is_valid_indexed_attestation (L765-779) forces sorted/unique attesting indices under a verified aggregate BLS signature so a validator's inclusion in a quorum cannot be forged or double-counted. process_attester_slashing (L1985-1998) computes the intersection of the two attestations' attesting_indices and calls slash_validator (L1249-1276, sets validator.slashed=True and burns effective_balance) on every index in that intersection that is_slashable_validator (L737-743). The proof holds: given valid conflicting-quorum evidence, the intersecting validators are slashed. The only gap is that slashing requires someone to submit the AttesterSlashing before an offending validator's withdrawable_epoch elapses (is_slashable_validator returns False afterward) -- this bounded-accountability window is the documented, intentional design of Casper FFG's weak-subjectivity model, not an implementation defect.
